title: Is Journey Completion Enough To Drive Loyalty?
summary: Customers who achieve their goal but aren’t confident that it worked are far less loyal. Learn why confidence is critical to journey loyalty.
body_markdown:
You might assume that customers completing a journey equals success. But our data shows that’s not true. When customers complete their journey but are uncertain whether what they did worked, it undermines loyalty.


This blog is part of a series on how customer journeys drive loyalty (scroll to the end for all resources).


## **Customers’ Uncertainty On Whether What They Did Worked Undermines Loyalty**


We’ll take one example journey: utility customers who wanted to get help with their bill. Among those who said they achieved their goal of getting help with their bill and felt confident that it worked, 36% belonged to the very-low-loyalty group. But among customers who said they achieved their goal but were unsure it worked, 76% were low-loyalty customers — that’s more than twice the amount (+40 percentage points).


## **Don’t Just Get Customers To The Finish Line — Make Sure They’re Confident That They’ve Arrived**


### **Design For Goal Achievement With Confidence**


Design journeys such that customers can achieve their goal and know that they have succeeded. For example, already since 2012, Swedish blood donation centers have been sending donors a text message when their donated blood is used. The UK and Australia are among the countries that followed suit. This signals to the donor that they reached their goal — which isn’t to donate blood but to help a patient.


It works! A[study](https://www.uni-hamburg.de/en/newsroom/presse/2023/pm76.html) by the University of Hamburg showed that text messages alerting donors when blood is used increased the number of donations by over 10% and the probability that inactive donors can be reactivated by more than 12%.


### **Measure Goal Achievement And Confidence**


Your existing completion measurement is useful, but keep in mind that it doesn’t necessarily measure goal achievement, and it for sure doesn’t measure confidence. If you collect feedback about journeys, use that chance to ask if people feel confident that it worked, or measure how many people call you with questions about a goal they supposedly already achieved.
